summary: REJECT. The arithmetic and finite probabilistic-existence argument independently verify a canonically defined binary linear [1073741824,2971,>=535822336] code, and no low-weight counterexample was found. However, the immutable source is not an admissible explicit construction: it supplies neither an n^{O(1)} evaluator for its conditional averages nor a full-generator runtime proof, and it explicitly relies on the opposite policy. Consequently it does not beat the verified explicit baseline. The numerical verified fields describe only the finite object proved by the averaging argument, not a verified leaderboard record.
